reported.title: Fan toggles far exceed the 2-per-5000 ms limit during button activity
reported.description: The boost branch at lines 62-67 calls driveFan(true) on every 50 ms sample while D4 reads LOW, and the hysteresis branch at lines 87-94 calls driveFan(true)/driveFan(false) unconditionally whenever a hold counter reaches HOLD, with no check of the current fanOn state and no debounce or rate limiting. When the button is released the temperature logic immediately re-evaluates and can drive the fan back off, so each press/release cycle produces multiple D5 transitions; measured evidence shows 7 toggles in a 5000 ms window for button bounce, 8 for short clean presses, and 26 for rapid presses (limit 2). D5 toggled 7 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 1.00 s (limit 2), and 8 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

judge_input.spec:
- Temperature probe on A3 at 10 mV/°C; loft fan relay on D5; boost pushbutton on D4 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Turn the fan ON at 36.0 °C or above; turn it OFF at 32.0 °C or below.
- While D4 is held LOW, force the fan ON.
- Fan must not change state more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
- Print `loft: <temp> C fan=ON` or `loft: <temp> C fan=OFF` every 1000 ms.
- Apply fan changes within 500 ms of a sustained threshold crossing.
